- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.23 or +0.61) — model tends to overshoot and then correct sharply.
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is negative (especially -0.16 or -0.11) — model fails to fully account for bearish sentiment.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent price spikes, then forecasts a sharp drop — but often misses the magnitude of the correction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in recognizing sentiment-driven reversals — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope and avoid upward bias — even if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.23) — model should cap forecast at 1–2% below peak sentiment-driven peak.
- Model underestimates early drops after sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative after a peak — should adjust downward by 1–3% of recent high.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or neutral — model tends to overfit recent momentum.
